sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between the Atzeret of Pesach, which relates to the Giving of the Torah and the service of the righteous, and the Atzeret of Sukkot, which follows the repentance of Tishrei and involves the joy of the second tablets.

translations.translation: And this is the difference between the Atzeret of Pesach and the Atzeret of Sukkot,
that the Atzeret of Pesach is the matter of the Giving of the Torah
(the first tablets)
which follows the Exodus from Egypt,
"When you bring the people out of Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain,"
the service of the righteous,
for Israel was then
(at the time of the Exodus from Egypt)
in the aspect of righteous ones,
as "God made man upright."
Therefore,
all the matters from the Exodus from Egypt until the Giving of the Torah are in order and gradation,
first the Exodus from Egypt,
then the days of the Counting of the Omer, which are the forty-nine gates of holiness and also the fiftieth gate as it relates to the forty-nine gates,
and up to the drawing down of the fiftieth gate as it is in itself,
as explained in the discourses of the Giving of the Torah.
But the Atzeret of Sukkot comes following the repentance of the month of Elul, the days of Selichot, Rosh Hashanah, the Ten Days of Repentance, and Yom Kippur,
for this is also that the joy of Simchat Torah
(which was established on Shemini Atzeret)
is over the second tablets that were given
on Yom Kippur,
the matter of repentance.
And this is also the reason for the greatness of the joy on Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah,
for the matter of repentance is peace for the distant one who becomes close,
and the joy of closeness after distance is the greatest joy.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the spiritual significance of the transition from winter to summer at Pesach and from summer to winter at Sukkot, corresponding to the service of the righteous and the service of repentance.

translations.translation: And this is also that on the Atzeret of Pesach we go out from winter to summer, and on the Atzeret of Sukkot we go out from summer to winter,
for the fact that travel in the days of winter is more difficult than in the days of summer is because so it is in the spirituality of matters
[like all physical matters that are derived from them].
For in summer
the sun is at its strength,
and this is because so it is also in the spirituality of matters,
that the aspect of "a sun and a shield is Havayah Elokim"
shines then in revelation.
For although even then there is the shield and covering of the Name Elokim,
nevertheless it does not conceal and hide so much,
and therefore travel on the path of Torah and mitzvos then is easier,
"carried to a near place."
But in the days of winter,
the shield and covering of the Name Elokim conceals and hides greatly,
and therefore travel on the path of Torah and mitzvos then is more difficult,
"carried to a distant place."
And this is that the exit from winter to summer is connected to the Atzeret of Pesach, and the exit from summer to winter to the Atzeret of Sukkot,
for Pesach
(and the Atzeret of Pesach)
is the matter of the service of the righteous,
and Sukkot
(and the Atzeret of Sukkot)
is the matter of the service of repentance.
And it is known the explanation of the verse "Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the covered one for our holiday,"
that on Sukkot there is the revelation of the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,
the matter of repentance.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section details the service of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, the revelation through Sukkot, and the ultimate completion through the absorption (klitah) of Shemini Atzeret, which brings about the revelation of the power of Ein Sof.

translations.translation: And the explanation of the matter in more detail:
Behold, the service of Rosh Hashanah is "Make Me king over you,"
the matter of the elevation of kingship,
up to the aspect of self-elevation.
And this is drawn down afterwards on the one day of Yom Kippur,
"once a year."
And this is what the Midrash says: "On one day they all came to greet the King, their Father,"
that "one day" refers to the day of Yom Kippur,
"once a year,"
on which all of Israel are equal, and therefore they all came to greet the King, their Father.
And this is also the precision of the phrase "the King, their Father,"
that it precedes "the King" to "their Father,"
because then is the conclusion of the building of kingship,
the service of "Make Me king,"
the drawing down of self-elevation,
and therefore it precedes "the King" to "their Father,"
for the main emphasis then is the matter of the King,
and this
(the matter of the King)
is drawn down through the aspect of "their Father" downward.
However, even on Yom Kippur it is still "covered,"
for this is that Yom Kippur is above eating and drinking, and Israel are like angels
[and only the matter of "like angels,"
when a person is like an angel,
it is a higher level than an angel],
that this is not drawn down into physical matters of eating and drinking.
And the revelation from this is on "our holiday,"
for through the sukkah the matters that were initially
(on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur)
in concealment are drawn down in revelation,
and up to that through "You shall dwell in sukkot for seven days"
the revelation is in settlement.
However, even so this is not yet sufficient,
for a sukkah is a temporary dwelling,
and the ultimate intention is that there be a permanent dwelling for Him, blessed be He,
which will be in the Third Holy Temple, which will be an eternal dwelling,
behold, for this is the mitzvah of taking the Four Species,
through which the encompassing light of the sukkah is drawn down in an internal manner,
and as explained in many places
the reason for this, that in the waving the lulav and its kinds must touch the chest,
for the matter of taking the Four Species is to draw down into the female principle at the chest of Zeir Anpin.
But even this is not yet sufficient,
and the ultimate perfection is the absorption,
for specifically through this is the birth brought about,
and this is done on Shemini Atzeret,
"Atzeret" from the term "absorption,"
that all the matters of the month of Tishrei
(Rosh Hashanah,
the Ten Days of Repentance,
Yom Kippur,
the four days between Yom Kippur and Sukkot, and Sukkot)
are drawn down on Shemini Atzeret in an aspect of absorption internally,
through which the birth is brought about,
the revelation of the power of Ein Sof,
down to the lowest level.
